To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Thank you for picking this up. Here are the details you asked for.

1. Terminals: BX-300. The four Embakasi depot terminals are on firmware 4.2.1, updated automatically from 4.1.8 on the night of 27 October. The two Mombasa Road terminals are still on 4.1.8 and their day-shift overtime exports correctly.

2. Shift template: NIGHT-8, 22:00 to 06:00.

3. Example: staff ID T-0417. Clocked in 21:54 on 30 October and out 06:07 on 31 October. The export split this into 2.1 hours REG on 30 October and 6.1 hours OT15 on 31 October. Expected: 8.0 hours REG and 0.2 hours OT15 (the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift, 8.2 hours in total after rounding to the tenth).

4. Export profile: Payroll CSV v2.

5. First noticed: 5 November 2026, while reviewing the draft October overtime. The problem appears to have started around 28 October, after the firmware update.

Impact: 38 night-shift staff are affected. The draft October overtime was overstated by about KES 212,000. We held those lines and corrected them by hand from the raw punches, but we cannot do that every month. The 4.2.1 release notes promised better midnight rollover handling, so this is the opposite of what we were told to expect.

We need either a fix or a clear workaround before November payroll inputs close on Friday 20 November. Kevin will test whatever you send.

Please also answer this directly: can our IT lead, Brian Ochieng, roll the four Embakasi BX-300 terminals back to 4.1.8 safely? He wants to know that the offline punch data stored on the devices will not be lost in the rollback. If it is not safe, please tell us what is.

Kind regards,

Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager, Tausi Freight
